description: [OWNER_QUEUE S-2] The update mechanism three FINISHED requirements depend on.
F-2 pinned every build version, F-8 every dependency, F-11 all 42 actions. Each
closed a real hole -- and each STOPS RECEIVING SECURITY FIXES the moment it is
pinned. That trade was accepted deliberately and written into the scripts; this
is the half that makes it sustainable. Without it the pins rot and the repo ends
up LESS safe than before they were added.
NO AUTOMERGE, deliberately: the queue says review-required, and a bot that merges
its own PRs is the kind of unattended write path F-11 spent its time removing.
AMENDED 2026-09-05 (ADR 067 decision 4). The clause above stands for MAJORS and
for anything that reaches a user. It is narrowed for patch, pin and digest
updates, which now automerge THROUGH ci-gate: the write path is not unattended,
it is gated by the single required status check on main, with enforce_admins on.
What was actually costing safety was the opposite of a bot merging too much - 16
updates sat under Awaiting Schedule and a config error stopped every PR for days
while the workflow reported 100% success (issue #420). A pin nobody advances is
the hole F-2 opened; ci-gate is what makes closing it cheap.
The prose that used to live here as a key called _scheduleWhy - which is not a
Renovate option, so Renovate refused the WHOLE config and opened no pull request
from 2026-09-03 - is now docs/ci/README.md section 8. `description` is a real
option and is the only place prose belongs in this file.
THROUGHPUT (O-RENOVATE-BACKLOG-OUTRUNS-ITS-LIMITS), measured 2026-09-22. The queue under
Awaiting Schedule on #417 grew from 16 entries (2026-09-03) to 21: 12 new branches in 19.0 days,
about 4.4 a week, read from the issue's edit history. Renovate opens PRs only inside the Monday
window, and exactly TWO runs land in it each week: the platform Worker's dispatch near 06:00Z
and this repository's daily cron, delivered 07:43-08:24Z. The old prHourlyLimit 2 therefore
capped the week at 4 PRs - the PRs actually opened were 4, 3 and 4 on the Mondays of 7, 14
and 21 September - against 4.4 arriving: the queue could only grow. THE BOTTLENECK IS
prHourlyLimit x the two runs per window; prConcurrentLimit 3 bound once (14 September).
New limits: drain the 21 over three Mondays (7 a week) on top of 4.4 arriving = 11.4 a week,
over two runs = prHourlyLimit 6. prConcurrentLimit is hourly x runs = 12, so majors the first
run opens and that wait for a hand merge never starve the second run.
The schedule stays `on monday`: one review window a week is the S-2 design, and the limits,
not the window, were what fell short. These limits assume BOTH runs: if the Worker target
(services/platform/src/scheduled.ts, workflow renovate.yml) is removed, Monday capacity halves
and the limits must be re-derived. A reader of #417 that goes red when the queue outruns them
is the second half of O-RENOVATE-BACKLOG-OUTRUNS-ITS-LIMITS and lands separately.
PR BODY (2026-09-29). Renovate writes its own PR body, and tooling/ci/assert-pr-rows.mjs fails a body
with no `Rows:` line: every dependency PR opened since the guard landed (2026-09-25) was red. The guard
stays universal; prBodyNotes gives every Renovate body the `none` form. Tests: tooling/ci/test/pr-rows.test.mjs.
prBodyNotes: Rows: none — Renovate dependency bump; no register row moves

description: Security fixes bypass the weekly window entirely.
osvVulnerabilityAlerts (above), 2026-10-01 [rv2-security-004 part 3]: Renovate also reads the OSV
database itself, for every manager it extracts (npm and pub here), and raises the fix PR with THESE
settings - labels, and outside the Monday window - on renovate.yml's daily cron. vulnerabilityAlerts
alone reads GitHub's Dependabot alerts, which had raised none on pubspec.lock, ever (dependabot.yml).
It is the PR half; the gate half is ops-watch's daily dependency-advisories scan of main.
EXPERIMENTAL in Renovate's own docs. RE-CHECK BY 2027-01-01: that an OSV-sourced PR has opened (or
that none was due), and that the option is still named and not yet a default; then drop this line.
Patch, pin and digest updates automerge, gated on ci-gate. automergeType is
the DEFAULT pr, never branch: ci.yml runs on push to main and on pull_request, so a
Renovate branch carries no status check of its own and a branch automerge
would be merging on the absence of a red rather than the presence of a green.
Majors and minors keep automerge: false from the top level.

packageRules.description: Actions move together and are low-risk to review as one PR.

description: mason_cli gets its own PR, never a group. Mason is what STAMPS APPS: an
unnoticed bump means the factory's own product can differ between runs with
nothing in the repo to explain it. Worth reading a dedicated PR for.
MAJOR PROPOSALS ONLY for the `java` and `node` toolchain floors. Both are declared
in tooling/versions.json as a BARE MAJOR on purpose, and that file says so itself in
$xcode_comment: 'THE VALUE IS A FLOOR, SO IT IS A MAJOR AND NOT A FULL VERSION ...
Same shape as `node` and `java` above, which are majors for the same reason.' The
installer resolves the patch at runtime, so a patch written into the PIN buys no
security fix at all -- it only moves a number nothing reads.
🔴 java PROVES IT, LIVE AND TODAY: PR #316 'update dependency java to v17.0.20+8'
rewrote tooling/versions.json ALONE and is RED on ci-gate. It is UNFIXABLE rather
than merely unsynced, and that distinction is the whole reason for this rule.
tooling/ci/assert-version-consistency.mjs was WIDENED on 2026-08-17 from 3 java call
sites to 8, and ALL FIVE IT GAINED CANNOT EXPRESS A PATCH IN ANY SYNTAX:
`JavaVersion.VERSION_17` (x2) and `JvmTarget.JVM_17` are ENUM CONSTANTS -- there is
no VERSION_17_0_20 -- while `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` and `java-17-openjdk-amd64` are
an apt package name and a JVM directory. Three of the five decide what the Android
build EMITS (class-file version, Kotlin JVM target); the other two decide which JDK a
local WSL build runs on at all. Only the 3 ORIGINAL `java-version:` inputs could even
hold `17.0.20+8`, and they merely choose which JDK is installed. A proposal that five
call sites cannot accept is a PR that can only ever be closed by hand, forever.
⚠️ node IS PROPHYLACTIC HERE, AND STATING THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT -- do not let a
later reader flatten the two into one proven case. Its 18 call sites are all
`node-version:` inputs, which CAN carry a full version, and node has never been
proposed at all: 0 of the 11 chore/renovate-* PRs ever opened name it. So node is NOT
a reproduced defect and this half of the rule has never fired. What node has is the
identical DESIGN -- a declared major floor whose installer resolves the patch --
differing only in that its customManager below carries `versioningTemplate: node`
while java's carries none. That asymmetry is the most likely reason java got PR #316
and node did not, but it is INFERRED FROM THE PR RECORD, NOT MEASURED: nothing here
ran Renovate. Either way the exposure is one deleted line away, and this rule makes
the intent survive that edit rather than depend on it.
Matched on `matchDatasources` because those two ids are declared in THIS file, on the
customManagers below, so the binding is checkable by reading one screen -- a manager
id or a glob would be a guess. MAJORS ARE NOT SUPPRESSED: 17 -> 21 is precisely the
change a human must land across all eight sites in one commit.
⏱ 2026-09-27: for java that sentence is SUSPENDED until a review on 2026-10-26 by the dated
java-majors rule near the end of packageRules; for node it stands.
glitchtip_cli gets its own PR and a needs-manual-check label, never a group. Its pin has TWO halves
in tooling/versions.json — the version and the sha256 of the release asset — and Renovate can move
only the first. Every proposal therefore arrives RED at deploy-web.yml checksum step until a human
downloads the new binary and writes its digest. Labelling it says so on the PR instead of leaving
the next reader to rediscover it from a failing job log.
Surfaced, never routine.

packageRules.description: Dev-only tooling can travel together; it cannot reach users.

description: melos: ONE branch for every manager that writes a melos copy (O-RENOVATE-BUMP-CANNOT-REACH-A-PINNED-COPY).
The pub manager writes pubspec.yaml's dev_dependency and would otherwise land on the dev tooling branch
while the regex managers land on chore/renovate-melos-*, and each branch is red without the other.
Must stay AFTER the dev tooling rule: a later groupName wins. assert-renovate-reach.mjs checks the order.
wrangler: ONE branch for every manager that writes a wrangler copy. github-actions writes each
wranglerVersion input (github actions group), npm writes the app brick's package.json (dev tooling),
the regex manager writes tooling/versions.json, npm writes the tooling/wrangler island (2026-09-24) -
each red alone. Must stay LAST among rules that set groupName for wrangler.
gitleaks is a HAND DECISION, declared here as well as in propagate-versions.mjs HAND_ONLY:
tooling/ci/scan-secrets.mjs VALIDATED_AGAINST names the release its output parser was checked
against, and only a human re-running that check may move it. A bump therefore lands red at
scan-secrets.mjs by design; this label says so on the PR. matchDepNames because the depName
is the versions.json key. assert-renovate-reach.mjs cross-checks this rule against HAND_ONLY.
The built-in github-actions manager must not propose runner labels or setup-java / setup-node
versions: those inputs are copies of tooling/versions.json keys (runner_ubuntu, java, node), and a
proposal that rewrites the copy and not the declaration is red by construction and poisons the
github actions (major) group it travels in. Observed on Dependency Dashboard #417, read 2026-09-21:
ubuntu 24.04 -> 26.04 and the setup-java major, both under the github-actions manager. The
versions.json customManagers still propose java and node majors; runner_ubuntu is an owner decision.
dev.flutter.flutter-plugin-loader is not a Maven or Gradle Plugin Portal artifact: the Flutter SDK
serves it through pluginManagement includeBuild("$flutterSdkPath/packages/flutter_tools/gradle") in
apps/subscriptiontracker/android/settings.gradle.kts, so the code that runs is whatever the Flutter
SDK pin (tooling/versions.json key flutter) ships, and no registry holds a newer version to propose.
Renovate's gradle manager looked it up anyway and #417 carried the failure under Repository
Problems (maven lookup, no-result; read 2026-09-22). Disabled here with that named reason: a
Flutter SDK bump is what advances it.
EVERY MAJOR WAITS FOR APPROVAL ON THE DEPENDENCY DASHBOARD (2026-09-27, O-RENOVATE-BACKLOG-OUTRUNS-ITS-LIMITS;
the Renovate drain triage of 2026-09-26). A major is a migration: a lane lands it by hand, or a person ticks
its ONE approve box on #417. Never 'create all'.
WHY NOW. With prHourlyLimit 6 and prConcurrentLimit 12, and the non-majors drained by the hand trains, the
Monday window of 2026-09-28 would spend its slots on the ten majors on #417, and at least six of them are red
BY CONSTRUCTION on main: java (Renovate reaches 1 of its 8 call sites), package_info_plus 10 (pub cannot solve
its win32 ^6 beside flutter_secure_storage_windows 3.x), flutter_riverpod 3, go_router 18, jose 6 (KeyLike in
the tests) and flutter_secure_storage 11 (compileSdk 37). A wall of red Renovate runs reads as failed deploys,
and each open PR holds a concurrency slot the next patch needs.
WHY THIS HIDES NOTHING. An update behind approval is listed on #417 with an `approve-branch` marker, which
tooling/ops/check-renovate-backlog.mjs COUNTS (WAITING_KINDS), and its age follows the branch name across the
move from Awaiting Schedule, so the backlog alarm keeps its whole memory. Security fixes are not held:
Renovate documents that vulnerability remediation PRs are still created without approval
(docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/dashboard, read 2026-09-27). Patch, pin, digest and minor updates are
untouched by this rule.
java MAJORS ARE DISABLED: POSTPONED 2026-09-27, REVIEW ON 2026-10-26, or sooner when `java` is split into a
runner JDK and a bytecode target (the drain triage of 2026-09-26, item M9). This SUSPENDS, for java only, the
'MAJORS ARE NOT SUPPRESSED' sentence of the java/node rule above; node majors are still surfaced.
WHY. The `java` customManager rewrites tooling/versions.json and nothing else, while
assert-version-consistency.mjs holds eight call sites to it and five of them cannot take a bot's edit (the
enum constants and the apt and JVM directory names named in the rule above). So chore/renovate-java-25.x is
red by construction for ever: no Monday can drain it, and while it is listed the backlog alarm's age limb
cannot turn green (24.1 days waited on 2026-09-27). On merit the Android bytecode target stays 17 (the
triage read developer.android.com/build/jdks: its Android-to-Java table tops out at API 34 / Java 17); what
can move is the JDK that runs Gradle and CI, once one key no longer drives both. Temurin 17 is supported at
least until Oct 2027 (adoptium.net/support), so nothing is at risk before the review date.
🔴 java IS NOW GENUINELY UNADVANCED, AND ONE GUARD CANNOT SEE IT. tooling/ci/assert-update-coverage.mjs reads
the customManagers and never packageRules, so it still reports `java` as covered by the manager below. That
green is not coverage until the review date: the rule above disables java's patch and minor proposals and
this one its majors, so nothing proposes any java version at all.
flutter_secure_storage IS HELD BELOW 11 (2026-09-27) until the 10.x migration has SHIPPED in a release and
compileSdk 37 has landed (the drain triage of 2026-09-26, items M7 and M7b). Upstream's 11.0.0 changelog
(pub.dev, read 2026-09-27, paraphrased): what was saved with the algorithms v10 deprecated is unusable after
the upgrade, so an app on a version before 10 must ship 10 first for the data to migrate; and 11.0.0 raised
compileSdk to 37, while apps/subscriptiontracker/android/app/build.gradle.kts pins compileSdk 36 on purpose.
So 9 -> 11 in one step is the one proposal that can lose what a signed-in user has stored.
WHY THIS HIDES NOTHING. allowedVersions narrows the proposal to 10.x, which is still a MAJOR: it waits for
approval under the rule above and check-renovate-backlog.mjs counts it like any other. Its branch becomes
chore/renovate-flutter_secure_storage-10.x, so its age restarts at the first dashboard that lists it; the
11.x entry's age is not carried over.
Second and third copies of the melos pin: the ci.yml workspace-gate install line and the README install
line (O-RENOVATE-BUMP-CANNOT-REACH-A-PINNED-COPY). SAME depNameTemplate as the versions.json manager above
on purpose, so all copies share one branch; the pubspec.yaml copy joins it through the melos group rule.
⏱ 2026-10-01: a fourth copy, the time-travel.yml Dart leg's install line, which runs the workspace gate's
own `melos run test` and so must move with it (tooling/ci/test/renovate-reach.test.mjs T1 found it unreached).
tooling/versions.json - wrangler [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
🔴 ADDED 2026-08-02 because tooling/ci/assert-update-coverage.mjs found it uncovered on its
very first run. wrangler is THE TOOL THAT PUBLISHES PRODUCTION, and $wrangler_comment in
versions.json records that it was already caught a full MAJOR version behind, chosen by a
third party's default, holding the account API token. It was declared once and advanced by
nobody: the npm manager reaches the ^4.0.0 range in each service's package.json, but nothing
reached this pin — and this pin is the value the deploy workflows actually install.
tooling/versions.json - glitchtip_cli [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-03 with the pin itself, so assert-update-coverage.mjs never sees it uncovered.
🔴 depNameTemplate AND packageNameTemplate DIFFER ON PURPOSE, and both halves are load-bearing.
assert-update-coverage.mjs keys its coverage map on depNameTemplate, so that must be the
versions.json KEY (glitchtip_cli) or the pin reads as advanced by nobody. Renovate gitlab-releases
looks up a PROJECT PATH, so packageName must be glitchtip/glitchtip-cli or it resolves nothing.
Collapsing the two breaks exactly one of those, silently — the house failure mode.
extractVersionTemplate strips the leading v: the project tags v1.0.0 and this file declares 1.0.0,
because the value is also spliced into a download URL as v<version>.
⚠️ A BUMP FROM THIS MANAGER LANDS RED BY DESIGN — glitchtip_cli_sha256 is the digest of the bytes
and Renovate cannot compute it. See $glitchtip_cli_comment and the $updateExemptions entry.
Second copy of the mason_cli pin: the ci.yml app-brick install line (O-RENOVATE-BUMP-CANNOT-REACH-A-PINNED-COPY),
and its third, the rehearse-app2.yml install line (the app #2 rehearsal stamps with the same mason).
SAME depNameTemplate as the tooling/versions.json manager above ON PURPOSE: Renovate puts upgrades with one
branch name on one branch, so every copy moves in one PR. tooling/ci/assert-renovate-reach.mjs proves it.
⏱ 2026-10-01: a fourth copy, the time-travel.yml brick leg's install line, which stamps the backend the way
ci.yml's app-brick job does and so must move with it.
tooling/versions.json - gitleaks [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-06 in the same change that moved the pin out of ci.yml's `env:` block, so
assert-update-coverage.mjs never sees it uncovered. Until then the secret scanner's version
was written inside a workflow, which is invisible to that guard: it was advanced by NOBODY
and no check in the tree could say so. A stale secret scanner does not go red, it goes
QUIET.
🔴 depNameTemplate AND packageNameTemplate DIFFER ON PURPOSE, exactly as for glitchtip_cli.
assert-update-coverage.mjs keys its coverage map on depNameTemplate, so that MUST be the
versions.json key; github-releases looks up an owner/repo, so packageName must be the repo.
Collapsing the two breaks precisely one of them, silently.
extractVersionTemplate strips the leading v: the project tags v8.30.1, this file declares
8.30.1, and ci.yml splices it back as v${ver} into the download URL.
⚠️ A BUMP FROM THIS MANAGER LANDS RED BY DESIGN - gitleaks_sha256 is the digest of the bytes
and Renovate cannot compute it. See $scanners_comment and the $updateExemptions entry.
tooling/versions.json - zizmor [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-06 with the pin's move out of ci.yml. Same shape and same reasons as the
gitleaks manager above; restated rather than cross-referenced because a description that
points at a neighbour outlives the neighbour's deletion.
zizmor is the workflow static analyser this repository's OWN workflows are scanned by, so a
pin nothing advances is the one that stops catching the next tj-actions-class compromise.
tooling/versions.json - osv_scanner [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-06 with the pin's move out of ci.yml.
🔴 THE KEY IS UNDERSCORED AND THE REPO IS HYPHENATED, and both spellings are load-bearing:
depNameTemplate must be `osv_scanner` because that is the versions.json key
assert-update-coverage.mjs looks for, and packageNameTemplate must be `google/osv-scanner`
because that is what GitHub resolves. This is the same trap the glitchtip_cli manager
records, one hyphen over.
OSV-Scanner is the ONLY scanner in this stack that reads pubspec.lock, and Play Console can
block updates on a vulnerable SDK version, so its currency has a store consequence.
tooling/versions.json - trivy [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-06 with the pin's move out of ci.yml. Same shape as the three managers above.
⚠️ THE matchString ANCHORS ON `"trivy":` WITH ITS CLOSING QUOTE, so it cannot capture
`"trivy_sha256":` — the digest key is exempted in $updateExemptions instead, because no
Renovate datasource resolves a checksum.
tooling/versions.json - trufflehog [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-06, one commit after the lane itself, because the first version of
.github/workflows/trufflehog.yml pinned the ACTION by SHA and left the SCANNER floating.
🔴 THE SHA PINS A WRAPPER, NOT A TOOL. trufflesecurity/trufflehog is a composite action whose
real step is `docker run "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}"`, and its `version` input defaults to
"latest" - so passing only `path` and `extra_args` runs a floating third-party image on a
public repository's full history, outside F-2 and outside this guard's reach. That is the
identical defect the gitleaks/zizmor/osv_scanner/trivy managers above were added to close,
one workflow over.
⚠️ THE GIT TAG CARRIES A LEADING `v` AND THE ASSET NAME DOES NOT (`v3.97.9` /
`trufflehog_3.97.9_linux_amd64.tar.gz`); extractVersionTemplate strips it.
⏱ 2026-09-30 [rv2-security-017]: the wrapper action is gone. trufflehog.yml installs the release
tarball through tooling/ci/install-pinned-tool.mjs against the sibling `trufflehog_sha256`, so a
bump from this manager lands RED at that install step until a human writes the new digest - the
same mechanism as the four scanners above. See $trufflehog_comment in tooling/versions.json.
tooling/versions.json - msstore_cli [pipeline F-2, 14]O-9
ADDED 2026-09-07 (phase 3 unit store-lanes, second pass), the same defect the retired web-ext key had: the
Microsoft Store submission transport was pinned to 0.4.2 inside the workflow that installs it and
nowhere assert-update-coverage.mjs could read.
🔴 THE GIT TAG CARRIES A LEADING `v` AND THIS FILE DOES NOT. Measured 2026-09-07 against
api.github.com/repos/microsoft/msstore-cli/releases/latest — tag_name `v0.4.2`, name `Microsoft Store
CLI v0.4.2`. extractVersionTemplate strips the prefix so versions.json keeps a bare 0.4.2, which is
the value `winget install --version` takes.
⚠️ THE MICROSOFT LANE CANNOT AUTHENTICATE YET (no Entra tenant exists), so a bump from this manager
is exercised by the dry-run path only until the owner creates one. That is a reason to WATCH the pin,
not a reason to leave it unwatched.
The Flutter FLOOR in every Flutter pubspec, `environment: flutter: ">=<flutter>"`
(O-PUBSPEC-FLOORS-UNTIED-TO-THE-PIN, 2026-09-25). assert-version-consistency.mjs holds each floor equal
to the versions.json `flutter` key, so a bump that moved versions.json alone would land red at every
Flutter pubspec; the SAME depName as the versions.json manager puts both writes on one branch, which is
the fix assert-renovate-reach.mjs names for a copy no bump reaches. The patterns are the workspace
members under packages/ and apps/ and the brick's app template. A pure-Dart pubspec has no floor and
matches nothing. The `sdk:` floor has no manager: `dart_language` is a $updateExemptions entry.
